issues.description: The UML in the problem statement defines numberOfLecturers as type int, but the solution implementation declares the attribute as byte (private byte numberOfLecturers). This mismatches the specified attribute type and may confuse students about the expected data type for lecturers.
issues.suggestedFix: Use the same data type across artifacts. Change numberOfLecturers in the solution (and template expectation) from byte to int so it matches the UML/problem statement (and update any dependent code accordingly).

issues.description: The setter for numberOfLecturers in the solution has a parameter of type byte (setNumberOfLecturers(byte)), while the problem UML and other getters imply an int should be used. This parameter type mismatch between specification and implementation can confuse students about the expected method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the setter signature with the UML: change setNumberOfLecturers parameter type from byte to int (and adjust the field type to int). Update the template TODO comments to indicate the int parameter to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The constructor in the solution defines the numberOfLecturers parameter as byte, whereas the UML in the problem statement indicates that numberOfLecturers should be an int. This constructor parameter type mismatch may mislead students when they implement the constructor following the UML order and types.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor parameter type for numberOfLecturers in the solution to int to match the UML and expected constructor signature. Also update the template guidance to reflect int for that parameter.
